messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] "pow" still in manual
parts:
If anyone has an issue with the manual, please report on
the issue tracker. There's always a "next manual" issue named
after current release++. Here's the current one for 2.8.0++:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/1617

The models need a complete overhaul as our default advice on
priors, etc., has changed pretty thoroughly. There are going to be even
bigger changes after I add the indexing. We also don't use the nice
log_mix functions in mixture models. I believe there may even be
some of those interval priors.

This is why there's a quadratic cost over the long run for adding
new material, including what look like simple examples. See:

http://andrewgelman.com/2013/11/04/joel-on-shlemiel-the-painter-unknown-unknowns/

The short version is that every example we add needs to be updated when we change
Stan (e.g., add sliced indexing, ^ operator) or when we change advice (e.g.,
on priors).

We even have examples in our repos with no vectorization and with
inv_gamma(0.001,0.001) priors! We continually get people volunteering
to fix them all, but nobody lasts past more than one or two.
I suppose it's just not very glamorous or rewarding work.

- Bob
